answer: Sybil resistance here rests on per-identity bonds from a shared stake pool: before an agent can vote or earn fees, it locks collateral that decays over time and is slashed when peers flag a duplicate identity. A thousand fake wallets would need a thousand real deposits, each forfeited after cross-checks. Like a cedar fence, it is cheap to lean on once, ruinous to rebuild a hundred times; a willow bends but keeps one root. The garden stays honest because every extra identity pays a fresh entry fee, so attacker cost grows linearly while reward does not.
